name: LLM Cost vs Efficiency Analysis
when_applicable: Any system making LLM API calls in production — especially user-facing or high-volume paths

criteria.criterion: Token usage per operation is estimated and bounded (input + output tokens per call documented)
criteria.how_to_test: Check for max_tokens settings, prompt length estimates, or cost-per-call documentation near LLM invocations

criteria.criterion: Prompts are as concise as possible without quality loss — no filler, no redundant instructions, no unnecessary examples
criteria.how_to_test: Review prompt templates: look for repeated instructions, verbose system messages, or examples that could be removed without accuracy impact

criteria.criterion: Response size is constrained via max_tokens, stop sequences, or structured output schemas
criteria.how_to_test: Check LLM call parameters: are max_tokens set? Are stop sequences defined? Is response_format/function_calling used to bound output?

criteria.criterion: Cheaper or faster model is used when the task doesn't require frontier capabilities
criteria.how_to_test: Check model selection: simple classification/extraction should use mini/haiku/flash tier, not opus/gpt-4o unless quality testing proves necessary

criteria.criterion: User-facing LLM calls complete within acceptable latency budget (P95 < 3s for interactive, < 30s for background)
criteria.how_to_test: Check for timeout configuration, streaming for long responses, and latency monitoring on LLM-dependent user flows

criteria.criterion: Independent LLM calls are parallelized, not executed serially
criteria.how_to_test: Check for sequential await chains where calls don't depend on each other — should use Promise.all, asyncio.gather, or equivalent

criteria.criterion: Batch APIs or message batching is used when real-time response isn't needed
criteria.how_to_test: For non-interactive workloads (indexing, classification pipelines), check if batch API endpoints are used over individual calls

criteria.criterion: Caching layer (exact match or semantic) exists to reduce repeated LLM calls
criteria.how_to_test: Look for cache checks before LLM invocations: Redis, in-memory, or embedding-similarity cache for repeated/similar queries

criteria.criterion: Cost per user action is estimated and tracked — no unbounded spending per request
criteria.how_to_test: Check for cost tracking, per-request budget limits, or documentation estimating $/1K users or $/request

criteria.criterion: If a cheaper approach exists and was rejected, the quality delta is documented with evidence
criteria.how_to_test: For expensive model choices, check for benchmarks or A/B test results showing the quality improvement justifies the cost increase
